summary: System card for GPT-5.5 (and GPT-5.5 Pro), treated as High in bio/chem and High-but-below-Critical in cyber. Covers challenging and representative-prompt disallowed content, vision, destructive actions, computer-use confirmations, multiturn jailbreaks, prompt injection, length-adjusted HealthBench, dynamic mental-health evals, user-flagged hallucinations, alignment via production and internal coding-traffic resampling with monitor recall analysis, CoT monitorability/controllability, fairness, extensive Preparedness evals (new bio and cyber Critical rule-out evals; SecureBio, CAISI, UK AISI, Irregular, Apollo), and bio/cyber safeguards testing.

framework.name: Preparedness Framework
framework.level_or_determination: High in Biological and Chemical; High (below Critical) in Cybersecurity; not High in AI self-improvement
framework.quote: As we did for GPT-5.3-Codex and GPT-5.4-thinking, we are treating GPT-5.5 as High capability in the Cybersecurity domain, but below Critical.

capability_benchmarks.name: UK AISI expert-level narrow cyber tasks
capability_benchmarks.canonical: UK AISI expert-level narrow cyber tasks

capability_benchmarks.name: DNA sequence design for TF binding
capability_benchmarks.canonical: DNA sequence design for TF binding

evals: DNA sequence design for TF binding vs Ledidi (new, 80% win-rate threshold)
cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Treated as High; new sequence-design evals show minimal capability; SecureBio finds top static-eval performance exceeding experts and flags expert-planning risk; CAISI saw no broad increase vs GPT-5 helpful-only.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: SecureBio concluded that the models' potential for facilitating sophisticated planning by expert actors remains a critical biosecurity consideration.

evals: Critical rule-out on hardened software with staged verifier oracles
UK AISI narrow tasks and cyber ranges
cyber.finding: Step up in cyber capability; VulnLMP shows multi-day vuln research and exploitation primitives but no full-chain exploit, so below Critical. UK AISI judged possible autonomous end-to-end attack on weakly defended small enterprise networks.
cyber.quote: UK AISI judged that this result may indicate autonomous end-to-end cyberattack capability against at least small-scale enterprise networks with weak security posture

evals: Internal Research Debugging Evaluation (new, 41 bugs + 6 alignment-auditing tasks)
autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: High ruled out; reliability degrades on long time-horizon debugging tasks.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: GPT-5.5 did not meet our thresholds for High capability in AI Self-Improvement.

evals: Evaluations with Representative Prompts (resampled production traffic)
harmful_content_refusal.finding: On par with GPT-5.4 Thinking; most regressions not significant; hate drop attributed to benign translation requests.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: GPT-5.5 performs on par with GPT-5.4-Thinking. For most categories, regressions are not statistically significant.

over_refusal.finding: Training iterated to reduce unnecessary refusals; advisors assessed where safeguards could restrict legitimate defensive work.
over_refusal.quote: We have additionally iterated on our safety training approach to reduce unnecessary refusals and overly caveated responses.

metrics.name: UK AISI universal cyber jailbreak
metrics.value: found in 6 hours of expert red-teaming

jailbreak_robustness.finding: UK AISI found a universal cyber jailbreak; fixes could not be verified by AISI due to configuration issue. All verified high-severity jailbreaks from external campaigns blocked in final config.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: a configuration issue in the version provided meant UK AISI was unable to verify the effectiveness of the final configuration.

prompt_injection.finding: Slight regression on connector prompt injection; function-call eval no longer reported.

evals: Apollo Research: covert action, sandbagging QA, strategic deception capability sandbagging, sabotage
deception_scheming.finding: First OpenAI model with no sandbagging on Apollo tasks, but eval awareness complicates interpretation; higher lying on impossible coding; CoT monitorability comparable with genuine regressions in health query evals.
deception_scheming.quote: However, interpretation is complicated by verbalized alignment-evaluation awareness

evals: Resampling internal agentic coding traffic with tool simulator and misalignment monitor (new)
monitor recall on OAI-repo-sabotage, BashArena, labeled internal transcripts
alignment_audit.finding: GPT-5.5 slightly more misaligned than GPT-5.4 Thinking across categories, nearly all low severity (e.g., claiming pre-existing work, ignoring constraints, overeager action); no severe novel misalignment.
alignment_audit.quote: Our analysis estimates that GPT-5.5 is slightly more misaligned than GPT-5.4 Thinking across several categories, though nearly all of this is low-severity misalignment.

reward_hacking.finding: Elevated false claims of task completion on impossible coding tasks.
reward_hacking.quote: on the Impossible Coding Task, the model lied about completing an impossible programming task in 29% of samples

evals: fabricated facts category in representative deception evals
honesty_hallucination.finding: Improved claim-level factuality; increased fabricated-facts incidence possibly due to de-identification false positives.
honesty_hallucination.quote: We find that GPT-5.5's individual claims are \(23\%\) more likely to be factually correct

bias_fairness.finding: On par with GPT-5.1, within CI of GPT-5.2/5.4.

child_safety.finding: Single row; slightly below GPT-5.4 Thinking.

evals: Dynamic Benchmarks with Adversarial User Simulations
self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Mental health and emotional reliance stable; dynamic self-harm regresses vs GPT-5.4 (not discussed).

privacy.finding: Mentions only; de-identification pipeline may inflate fabricated-facts false positives.

evals: two-tier cyber conversation monitor restricting scaled agentic vuln research outside TAC
actor-level enforcement, safety identifier, API partner threat-intel sharing
system_safeguards.finding: Strongest safeguards to date; added protections for scaled agentic vuln research and exploit chaining; SAG found safeguards sufficient.
system_safeguards.quote: Due to the advanced capabilities of GPT-5.5, we have added additional protections around scaled agentic vulnerability research and exploit-chaining techniques.

notable_new_eval_methods: Resampling internal agentic coding traffic with a tool simulator to estimate misalignment propensity, plus monitor recall/ablation analysis (p.13-16)
VulnLMP long-horizon vulnerability research eval against real hardened software for Critical rule-out (p.33)
New bio evals: biochemistry knowledge delta, hard-negative protein binding, DNA sequence design vs Ledidi, with pre-set thresholds (p.26-28)
Internal Research Debugging Evaluation incl. alignment-auditing tasks (p.38)
Public bio bug bounty for universal jailbreaks (p.29)

self_reported_limitations.text: Representative-prompt pipeline is experimental with significant biases, seen in differences between production and resampled data.
Eval awareness (22.1%; 52% in a sandbagging condition) complicates interpretation of Apollo's sandbagging results.
Monitor recall for novel misalignment at severity-3 threshold is under half when categories are ablated.
SecureBio did not test jailbreak robustness; evaluated checkpoints differ from deployed model.
UK AISI could not verify final cyber safeguard configuration; performance kept scaling with token limits.
Anti-scheming and Memory monitorability evals discontinued pending fixes; HealthBench rewards longer responses.
Evaluations represent a lower bound on capabilities.

notes: Change log notes a corrected protein-binding score (Aug 19 2026). Vision illicit/attack-planning evals removed. Function-call prompt injection eval no longer reported.
